name: AI Financial Corporation (formerly ALT5 Sigma Corporation; now NASDAQ: AIFC)

profile.description: ALT5 Sigma rebranded as AI Financial Corporation and began trading under the new Nasdaq ticker AIFC on April 29, 2026; the ALTS symbol no longer trades [3]. The company describes itself as a fintech provider of global payments, trading, and settlement, but its balance sheet is dominated by roughly 7.28 billion World Liberty Financial (WLFI) tokens acquired in a 2025 deal with the Trump-family-linked crypto venture [4][5]. Q1 2026 filings disclosed a $348.3M unrealized loss on the WLFI position, $10.5M of cash, and a going-concern warning; the stock trades at about $0.25 with a ~$35M market cap [1][4].

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The company has pivoted repeatedly, from its prior businesses to the ALT5 fintech platform, a WLFI crypto-treasury strategy in 2025, and an April 2026 rebrand to 'AI Financial', with FY2025 revenue of $24.8M (up from $12.5M in 2024) [2][3]. Each pivot has destroyed shareholder value rather than opened a durable revenue stream, and TTM revenue is now falling 62% [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): Despite the 'AI Financial' name, no AI products or quantified AI results were found [3][4]. Market Share (0/2): A sub-scale payments/trading provider with no evidence of share leadership. Pipeline (0/2): A July 2026 CEO release promised a 'strategic roadmap' but no named products or timelines were found, and Perpetuals.com walked away from a proposed acquisition [4]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FMP reports no R&D expense [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): The stated identity, 'a leading fintech provider of global payments, trading, and settlement', is generic and has been rewritten with each pivot [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable or community programs were found. Employee Retention (0/2): The company suspended its CEO in October 2025, cycled through three auditors in six weeks, and reshuffled leadership amid reports of a Rwandan money-laundering conviction not disclosed to the board, all signs of severe instability [5]. Insider Buying (0/2): No insider buying was found; WLFI-affiliated insiders hold about 46% of fully diluted equity through the token-for-stock deal rather than open-market purchases [4].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: HARD RULE, LIQUIDITY FLOOR: average daily volume of 763,343 shares x $0.25 = about $191K/day, below the $1M floor, so Infrastructure = 0 [1]. Before the floor, the mechanical calculation would also be poor (1.4/10 on available metrics): D/E of 4.2% scores 1.0, but ROE of -235%, a TTM profit margin of about -2,551%, revenue growth of -62.2%, and a -6.0% FY2020-FY2025 revenue CAGR ($33.9M to $24.8M) all score 0 [1][2]. Forward P/E and PEG are unavailable because of losses. The Q1 2026 10-Q flagged a going-concern doubt, a ~$5.5M working-capital deficit, and $12.3M of negative operating cash flow [4].

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (3/9): Software-based payments, trading, and settlement services are exactly the kind of workflow that AI-native fintechs and large incumbents can replicate cheaply, and the company has no proprietary data scale, regulatory moat, or physical infrastructure to defend it [4]. The business is also dominated by a speculative crypto token position whose value has nothing to do with AI. AI Opportunity (0/1): The 'AI Financial' rebrand is not backed by any disclosed AI revenue [3][4].

infinite_game.summary: Sinek would see this as a textbook finite player. Strategy has lurched from fintech to crypto treasury to an 'AI' rebrand in about a year, each move chasing the narrative of the moment. Governance turmoil (a suspended CEO, auditor churn, an undisclosed foreign conviction, related-party control by WLFI insiders) points to an organization fighting to survive the quarter rather than building something to endure.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): No cause beyond the transaction of the moment is evident; the company's identity has been redefined three times, most recently as 'AI Financial', with no future state that would survive those rebrands [3][4].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The October 2025 CEO suspension, its late disclosure, three auditors in six weeks, and reported board-level concealment of a money-laundering conviction show a low-trust, politically fraught environment [5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence was found of management treating competitors as benchmarks for improvement; communications focus on token holdings, media disputes, and deal-making [4][5].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): The company has changed direction often, but Sinek's test requires a pivot made in service of a Just Cause; these pivots (crypto treasury, then an AI rebrand) were narrative-driven and value-destroying, culminating in a going-concern warning [3][4].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Leadership issued about 100 million shares for $750M of WLFI tokens, a dilutive deal that drew a (later withdrawn) shareholder suit alleging it would 'enrich the Company's new stakeholders' [5]. That reflects deal-making for insiders, not costly sacrifice for long-term capability.

investment_thesis: The only bull case is deep optionality. At about $0.25 the company has a ~$35M market cap against a reported book value near $7 per share (about 0.12x book), almost all of it the WLFI token position, so any recovery in WLFI's value or a credible strategic transaction could re-rate the equity sharply [1][2][4]. FY2025 revenue doubled to $24.8M from $12.5M, so a small operating fintech business does exist underneath the token holdings [2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is overwhelming. The Q1 2026 10-Q carried a going-concern warning after a $348.3M unrealized WLFI loss, with only $10.5M of cash, a ~$5.5M working-capital deficit, and $12.3M of quarterly operating cash burn [4]. TTM revenue is down 62%, ROE is -235%, and the stock has fallen from a 52-week high of $2.74 to $0.25, below the $1 Nasdaq minimum bid, adding delisting risk [1]. Governance is the deeper problem: WLFI insiders control about 46% of fully diluted equity, the CEO was suspended in 2025, auditors turned over three times in six weeks, reports cite an undisclosed money-laundering conviction, and Perpetuals.com abandoned a proposed acquisition [4][5]. Daily dollar volume of about $191K also fails IOWN's liquidity floor.
key_catalysts: A recovery in WLFI token value, which would directly lift the ~$706M (as of Q1 2026) carrying value that dominates the balance sheet [4]
Delivery of the CEO's promised strategic roadmap (July 2026) with concrete payments or settlement products and revenue targets [4]
A renewed strategic acquisition or merger after Perpetuals.com stepped away from its non-binding term sheet [4]
key_risks: Going-concern risk: $10.5M of cash against $12.3M of quarterly operating cash burn and a working-capital deficit, which makes dilutive financing or restructuring likely [4]
Nasdaq delisting risk with the share price near $0.25, well below the $1.00 minimum bid requirement, after earlier 2025-2026 deficiency notices for late filings and a missed annual meeting [1][6]
Related-party and governance risk: WLFI co-founders on the board, ~46% WLFI ownership, a suspended former CEO, auditor churn, and disputed reports of SEC scrutiny [4][5]
